name: Question 8
problem:
Describe the set $S={4,24,144,864,...}$ using a constructive definition.

$$
\frac{2}{3}\cdot {6}^{n}
$$
worked_solution:
Notice that the elements of our set

$$
4,\,24,\,144,\,864,\,…
$$

form an infinite geometric sequence with a common ratio $r=6:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =6 \\  & =\frac{24}{4} \\  & =\frac{144}{24} \\  & =\frac{864}{144} \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $n$th term ${a}_{n}$ of our sequence for $n\in N,$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =4\cdot {6}^{n-1} \\  & =4\cdot {6}^{n}\cdot {6}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot {6}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can define our set using a constructive definition as follows:

$$
S={\frac{2}{3}\cdot {6}^{n}\,:\,n\in N}
$$

EXPLANATION

Notice that the elements of our set 4,24,144,864,… form an infinite geometric sequence with a common ratio r=6:

r=6=244=14424=864144=⋯

Therefore, the nth term an of our sequence for n∈N, is given by an=a1⋅rn−1=4⋅6n−1=4⋅6n⋅6−1=23⋅6n.

Therefore, we can define our set using a constructive definition as follows:

S={23⋅6n:n∈N}
